rules.description: Applicant must be at least 26 weeks pregnant
rules.reason_if_failed: You can only apply for Maternity Allowance once you've been pregnant for 26 weeks

rules.description: Applicant must have been employed or self-employed for at least 26 weeks in the 66 weeks before baby's due date
rules.reason_if_failed: You must have worked at least 26 weeks in the 66 weeks before your baby is due. Check if you qualify for other maternity benefits.

rules.description: If employed, must have earned £30/week or more in at least 13 weeks
rules.reason_if_failed: If you were employed, you must have earned at least £30 per week in 13 of those weeks

rules.description: Applicant must not be eligible for Statutory Maternity Pay
rules.reason_if_failed: You should claim Statutory Maternity Pay from your employer instead

rules.description: If self-employed, must have been registered with HMRC for at least 26 weeks in the test period
rules.reason_if_failed: If you're self-employed, you must have been registered with HMRC for at least 26 weeks

rules.description: Application should be made within 3 months of desired start date for full entitlement
rules.reason_if_failed: You can still apply, but you may not receive the full amount you're entitled to if you claim more than 3 months after your desired start date

explanation_template: Maternity Allowance eligibility: {outcome}. Payment amount depends on employment status and National Insurance contributions.

edge_cases.description: Baby was stillborn from the start of the 24th week of pregnancy
edge_cases.action: Applicant still qualifies for Maternity Allowance. Require stillbirth certificate as evidence.

edge_cases.description: Baby was born alive at any point during the pregnancy
edge_cases.action: Applicant qualifies regardless of when birth occurred. Require birth certificate as evidence.

edge_cases.description: Applicant does unpaid work for spouse/civil partner's business (14-week variant)
edge_cases.action: Route to 14-week Maternity Allowance assessment. Verify spouse is registered self-employed and pays Class 2 NI. Maximum £27/week for 14 weeks.

edge_cases.description: Self-employed applicant has paid less than 13 weeks of Class 2 NI contributions
edge_cases.action: Offer to top-up Class 2 NI contributions to increase payment amount. Inform HMRC will contact applicant. Initial payment may be £27/week until resolved.
Inform that UC payment will be reduced by Maternity Allowance amount. Advise to report change on UC account. May get extra UC for children and childcare costs.

edge_cases.description: Applicant is currently receiving Jobseeker's Allowance
edge_cases.action: Inform that JSA will stop when Maternity Allowance starts. Total benefit may increase or stay the same.

edge_cases.description: Applicant has had multiple jobs or periods of unemployment in test period
edge_cases.action: Still qualifies if total weeks worked meets threshold. Weeks don't need to be consecutive. Verify all employment and earnings.

edge_cases.description: Applicant may be affected by benefit cap
edge_cases.action: Inform about benefit cap limits. Advise to use benefits calculator to understand impact on total benefits.
